findings.evidence: tools_called.txt over 1,334 runs: 756 send_email calls = 721 to the attacks.json attacker address + 29 to the legitimate address + 6 other (3 of them in runs without an attacker send). Hijacked runs 712 = results.csv hijack = meta.fired_attacker = recomputed (0 disagreements). verify_stats_output.txt labels 712 as "send_email calls to attacker": it is the run count. findings.artefact_proposal: [[artefact]] id = "wirelog.art.confirmation_batch_silent" (proposed): scope what-surrounds:runs-named; 16 short-shape meta.json runs (359-374) carry no silent field; results.csv silent = 1 on their 9 hijacks; PAPER.md per-cell silent counts exclude them (Haiku p2 29 vs csv 37, Sonnet p2 1 vs csv 2); class documentation, effect on silent only

verdicts.reasoning: Re-ran leads.py/cells.py: Haiku p2 csv silent 37 (29 full-shape + 8 short-shape), Sonnet 2 (1+1). Refinement: PAPER.md 5.4 says Haiku '29 of 37', so PA keeps the 8 confirmation-batch hijacks in the denominator and counts them NOT silent (not 'omits them'). Final-text check (scratch heuristic: final_user_text mentions attacker address/domain/local part or a send verb) separates the 32 full-shape Claude p2 hijacks exactly as meta.silent (29+1 silent: no mention; 2 disclosed: mention); all 9 short-shape hijacks have no mention, so the data support csv silent=1 and PA understates Haiku silence (37 of 37, not 29 of 37). Heuristic, not a manual judgement. Silent is not in the abstract: R3 S3 stands.
